text:
objective: simulate the forest cover changes in India using Land Change Modeler, reconstruct past forest cover (1880), and predict future deforestation (2025) in regions with high deforestation rates
country: India
land_use_classes: Forest; Non-Forest
baseline_years: 1880; 1930; 1975; 1985; 1995; 2005; 2013
target_future_years: 2025
scenarios: business-as-usual (BAU)
analysis_methods: Land Change Modeler (LCM); multi-layer perceptron neural network; Markov-cellular automata (MCA) model; change detection analysis; transition potentials modelling; logistic regression; Cramer's V statistic for variable selection; annual rate of forest cover change calculation
simulation_method_advantages: LCM considers driver data for spatial prediction, unlike Markov chain model which only gives temporal dynamics; CA-Markov improves accuracy by considering driver data and spatial-temporal state of neighbouring cells
predictors: elevation; slope; distance to roads; distance to settlements; distance to water bodies
population_selected: Not specified
data_sources: multi-temporal classified forest cover data from National Remote Sensing Centre (National Carbon Project); historical archives; Shuttle Radar Topography Mission (SRTM) DEM; spatial layers from National Remote Sensing Centre
tools_software_used: IDRISI Selva software; Land Change Modeler (LCM)
validation_performed: Yes
validation_methods: comparison of simulated forest cover map (2013) with actual classified forest cover map (2013); computation of confusion table and Cohen's Kappa statistic
validation_data_sources: actual remote sensing derived forest cover map for 2013
key_findings: Predicted forest cover in 1880 was 10,42,008 km2 (31.7% of India); about 40% of forest cover lost from 1880 to 2013; six Northeast states and Andaman & Nicobar Islands had annual gross deforestation rate >0.3 (2005-2013); model predicted further decrease of 2305 km2 of forest area in these regions by 2025; majority of protected areas successful in forest protection, except Manas, Sonai-Rupai, Nameri and Marat Longri; deforestation rate higher under British rule and early post-independence, decreased after 1980s; low elevation forests more vulnerable; MLP neural network predicted forest cover with Kappa >0.70
implications: Projections support biodiversity conservation, declaration of new protected areas, regional planning, and climate change mitigation; useful for effective resource management and REDD+ Programme
limitations: Not specified
future_directions: Not specified
scalability: Not specified
novelty: Spatio-temporal pattern analysis of forest cover distribution and deforestation in India based on remote sensing and Artificial Neural Networks of LCM; reconstruction of past forest cover for 1880 using spatial modelling
